It is associated with the ancient sport of Sumo wrestling, which originated in Japan but has Hindu influences. The name is used for the wrestlers in the sport, symbolizing strength, power, and determination. Sumo wrestling is a cultural practice that showcases the rich heritage and tradition of India and Japan.

historical_references.reference: Sumo was a revered ancient Indian sage and Rishi, who is believed to have lived around 1500 BCE in the Rigvedic period. He is mentioned in several hymns of the Rigveda and is associated with the devas (gods) and Asvins, the gods of horses and fertility. Sumo is also believed to be the father of Sage Vasistha.

historical_references.reference: Sumo is also the name of a popular form of wrestling that originated in ancient India around 2000 BCE. This martial art was an integral part of Hindu culture and was considered a purifying ritual. Sumo wrestling involves two opponents trying to force each other out of a circular ring or pushing each other down to the ground.

modern_usage.modern_context: Sumo, a traditional Japanese sport with roots dating back over 1,500 years, has seen a modern resurgence in popularity. While its origins remain deeply rooted in Japanese culture, sumo is now enjoyed by fans all around the world. The Sumo Wrestling World Championships, held annually in Kyoto, Japan, attracts athletes and spectators from over 30 countries. The Japan Sumo Association, which governs the sport, has evolved its rules and scoring system to cater to a more global audience. Additionally, sumo has found a new platform in professional wrestling through All Japan Pro Wrestling, where it is often combined with elements of drama and spectacle to create a unique and engaging experience for fans.
